sections.title: NRN/CNTRL PLAINS INTO UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: OVERALL SEVERE WEATHER SCENARIO IS RATHER COMPLEX TODAY OWING TO PRESENCE OF SEVERAL WEAK PERTURBATIONS EMBEDDED WITHIN BROADLY ANTICYCLONIC MIDLEVEL FLOW REGIME IN PLACE ACROSS THE N-CNTRL TIER OF STATES. THIS BOUNDARY WILL LIKELY SERVE AS THE FOCUS FOR THE MOST CONCENTRATED STRONG TO SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE DIURNAL HEATING CYCLE. sections.title: SERN STATES
sections.text: 12Z SOUNDINGS FROM TLH/CHS INDICATE THE PRESENCE OF A VERY MOIST AIR MASS WITH 100-MB MEAN MIXING RATIOS OF NEAR 20 G/KG... CONTRIBUTING TO A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS. EARLY VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SUGGESTS THAT STRONG DIABATIC HEATING SHOULD OCCUR ACROSS MUCH OF AL/GA INTO SRN SC AND FL...SUPPORTING MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY WITH MLCAPE OF 2500-3500+ J/KG. PRIMARY FACTOR DISTINGUISHING TODAY FROM SATURDAY IS THE EARLY PASSAGE OF MIDLEVEL TROUGH AXIS OFF THE ATLANTIC COAST WITH GENERALLY RISING MIDLEVEL HEIGHTS THROUGH THE REMAINDER OF THE DAY. AS SUCH...THE POTENTIAL FOR MORE ORGANIZED SEVERE WEATHER APPEARS TO HAVE DIMINISHED OVER THE PAST 24 HOURS...THOUGH ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGER STORM CLUSTERS. ..MEAD/SMITH.. 08/01/2010
